transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi… um, I guess what brought me in is work stuff, mostly. I try really hard to do things right, but I keep starting the sanitation steps, or the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, and then somehow I miss the last part or don’t fully finish it. Even when I know it’s important and, honestly, that my job depends on it being done correctly.

I don’t mean to be careless—I really don’t. It just keeps happening, and I figured I should probably ask for help instead of pretending it’s fine.
Do you feel anxious or worried when you're working on these tasks?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I mean, I don’t think I feel anxious exactly while I’m doing them—at least not in a way I’ve really noticed. I mostly just try to get through the steps and do it right.

I do worry afterward sometimes, like wondering if I missed something, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean. Does that answer it okay?
Do you have recurring thoughts or urges that you feel compelled to respond to or act on?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in the sense of like, a thought that I have to do something because of it. I mean, I can overthink whether I finished something correctly, but I don’t have urges or routines I feel forced to do, if that’s what you mean.

Sorry, I’m not sure if I’m answering that the right way.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted while working on tasks?

Yeah… I think so. I try not to make it sound like I’m just not paying attention on purpose, because I really am trying. But even when I start a shift telling myself to stay focused, after a while the cutting and weighing and checking labels all kind of blur together.

Sometimes I’ll realize I’ve been looking at the same tray or the log sheet and I’m not actually taking in what I’m supposed to do next. It’s embarrassing to say, but yes, I do get distracted or kind of lose the thread pretty easily. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel overwhelmed or upset when you realize you've made a mistake at work?

Yeah… I do. I try not to make a big scene about it, but when I realize I’ve messed something up at work, I get really upset with myself.

It’s not just like, “oh, I made a small mistake.” It’s started to feel more serious because I’ve had to have retraining meetings, and sometimes coworkers have to cover parts of what I was supposed to be doing. I know everyone makes mistakes, but I worry they’re going to think I can’t handle being on the line.

I guess I’m scared I’m becoming more of a safety concern than a reliable worker. And I really don’t want that. I’m worried they’ll move me somewhere else or just fire me. Sorry, I don’t mean to sound dramatic. That’s just kind of where my mind goes when it happens.
Do you often feel worthless or inadequate outside of work?

I don’t know if I’d say worthless… that feels like a strong word. Outside of work I can feel kind of… behind, I guess, or not as put together as other people my age. But I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

It’s more like I get embarrassed with myself when I don’t handle things the way I think I should. I’m not sure if that counts as inadequate, though. Is that what you mean?
Do you have trouble paying attention in other areas of your life, outside of work?

Yeah… I think so, although the easiest example is still work, honestly. Like, even when I start a shift really trying to stay locked in, after a while the cutting, weighing, and checking labels all sort of blur together.

Then I’ll catch myself just staring at the same tray or the log sheet, and I’m not really taking in what I’m supposed to do next. I know that’s work, not outside work, sorry… but it’s the clearest way I can explain the attention thing.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with friends or family because of your difficulties with focus or making mistakes?

Not really… at least, I haven’t noticed anything major. I mean, I’m sure I can be a little distracted sometimes, but I don’t think my friends or family would say it’s caused big problems.

Maybe I miss little things or need reminders, but I don’t think it’s been like work, where there are actual consequences. I hope that answers what you’re asking.
Do you think your difficulties with completing tasks and making mistakes are related to worrying about something bad happening?

I’m not sure… I don’t think it’s usually because I’m worried something bad will happen. I mean, sometimes I do get nervous after I’ve already made a mistake, because I don’t want anyone to be upset with me or think I’m careless.

But before it happens, it doesn’t really feel like I’m thinking, “Oh no, something bad is going to happen.” It’s more like I just lose track or don’t finish things the way I meant to. Does that make sense?
Do you have any recurring, intrusive thoughts that disturb you?

Um… I don’t think so. Not in the way that sounds, like thoughts that keep coming in and really disturb me.

I mean, I can get stuck thinking about things I need to do or wondering if I forgot something, but I wouldn’t call it intrusive or scary. Unless you mean something different by that?
Have your difficulties with completing tasks and making mistakes affected your overall quality of life?

Yeah… I think it has, mostly because of work. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but there have been formal retraining meetings, and sometimes coworkers have to cover parts of what I’m supposed to be doing.

That’s been really embarrassing. I worry I’m becoming more of a safety concern than a reliable worker, and I’m scared they might move me off the line or even fire me if it keeps happening. So… yes, I guess it has affected my quality of life more than I like to admit.
Have you had difficulties with completing tasks and paying attention since you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to blame everything on being a kid or make it sound dramatic, but my mom still has some of my elementary school report cards, I think from around fourth grade, that said I was bright but needed constant reminders to finish classwork and turn in homework.

I remember understanding the lessons okay, but if the teacher gave a bunch of instructions, I’d miss parts of them unless she was kind of nearby or checking in on me. So… yes, I guess it has been there since I was younger.
